description: Striving to create an innovative app that can show our growing SPHEREx sky data in a easy to see visual format, allowing easier discovery space objects.
summary: SPHEREx Skyviewer allows you to browse around the sky as if you would look at the Earth on google maps. You can pick a point in the sky and search for SPHEREx data from that spot, enter your own coordinates, or the name of the object you'd like to see!
details:
Watch the infrared sky change. A web app for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Pick a star and step through every SPHEREx exposure of it, aligned onto one grid and labelled with each frame's wavelength and quality, so a change you see is a real change in the sky

  • Interactive homepage. A 3D SPHEREx model with a beam that scans 0.75–5 µm, the five challenge targets, and a short explainer of how SPHEREx sees.
  • Full-sky viewer. Pan and zoom, search any object by name (via CDS SIMBAD) or by RA Dec, or lock onto the crosshair.
  • Time-lapse player. Every SPHEREx exposure of the region, sorted by date, with play/pause, scrubbing and speed control.
  • All six detectors (D1–D6) as layers, each showing only its own frames, so the date always matches the image.
  • Target panel with what the object is, what to expect, its motion and distance, and what the current frame measured.
  • Shareable links like ?target=wise0855 or ?ra=133.76&dec=-7.24&fov=0.15, which open the viewer directly and work when embedded.
